item.title: Eisenkot: I will not allow any delay to swearing in of Knesset
item.description:
Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot accused Likud and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of conducting a "coordinated and organized campaign to delegitimize the election results," stressing that he would not allow any delay in the swearing-in of the Knesset.
Eisenkot announced that his teams were preparing to submit bills when the Knesset convenes, adding: "The days when Netanyahu used the institutions of government against Israel's interests and for his own personal needs are over."

item.title: Shin Bet clarifies election probe: No evidence came from political parties
item.description: Shin Bet says its election probe is based on independently gathered intelligence, rejects speculation, and warns against blaming the entire Arab sector.

item.title: Crisis and historic low: "Shas is not a one-man party"
item.description: Former MK Nissim Ze'ev, one of the founders of Shas, is not surprised by the crisis facing the party. He criticizes its poorly managed election campaign and Aryeh Deri's exclusive control over the party.

item.title: Haredi party leader admits election failure: 'I failed, but we'll be back'
item.description: After receiving 10,000 votes in elections, Moti Leitner takes responsibility for party's election defeat, acknowledges campaign mistakes, and vows to continue fighting for change within haredi society.

item.title: Eisenkot and Golan meet following elections
item.description:
Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot and Democrats party chairman Yair Golan met on Thursday to discuss the election results.
A statement said: "During the meeting, the two also discussed their shared commitment to fulfilling the will of the voters as quickly as possible."

item.title: Following Flydubai hijacking: Airlines required to submit crew details in advance
item.description: Following the Flydubai security lapse, authorities have decided to revise airline regulations, requiring carriers to submit crew members' details 48 hours before departure.

item.title: Draft dodgers arrested, haredi protests set to disrupt traffic
item.description: Following the arrests of two yeshiva students, the Jerusalem Faction plans mass protests as police prepare to close Highway 4 and other roads near Bnei Brak.

item.title: Double-envelope ballot counting has concluded
item.description:
The Central Elections Committee announced that the counting of double-envelope ballots has been completed.
So far, results from 12,644 polling stations have been entered into the system, totaling 5,589,836 votes. Of these, 5,564,764 are valid votes and 25,072 are invalid.

item.title: President Herzog calls King of Spain following deadly train crash
item.description:
President Isaac Herzog called King Felipe VI of Spain to express his deep condolences following the deadly train collision in Spain on Wednesday.
During the call, President Herzog conveyed his heartfelt sympathy to His Majesty the King, the families of the victims, and the Spanish people, and he wished a full and speedy recovery to all those injured.

item.title: Following Flydubai security lapse: Airlines to be required to report crew details in advance
item.description:
Following the Flydubai security lapse, authorities have decided to revise the guidelines for airlines, which will now be required to submit their crew members' details 48 hours before departure.
The new guidelines are intended to allow advance screening of crew members and prevent similar incidents from recurring.
